system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Seller Package Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material term. Several of its positions are our conditional fallbacks (the 20% / AUD 4.8m cap and the 18-month claims period), which we cannot concede without Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. None has been given. Two positions go further and conflict with our non-negotiables: the Fundamental/Title regime and the fraud carve-out. The Seller's disclosure letter also confirms that several conditions (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay payment, bonuses) remain unsatisfied as at 22 September 2026. The data is six weeks old, so we should request a bring-down.

## 1. Issue-by-issue comparison

| Area | Seller position | Playbook | Pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m (4.8m only as conditional fallback with Frost's written approval) | Open at 25%/6m. Do not concede without written authority. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, deductible (excess only) | AUD 50,000, tipping (first dollar once exceeded) | Reject. Reinstate tipping basket. |
| General claims period (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months (18 only as fallback with approval) | Reject. Reinstate 24 months. |
| Limitation applies to all claims | "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" | Separate regimes; no hidden general override | Delete. Carve out Fundamental/Title and fraud. |
| Fundamental/Title | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | Reject outright. Non-negotiable. |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to all Claims "of any nature" | Carve out fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct to the maximum extent enforceable | Add carve-out. Non-waivable. |
| Disclosure (Sch. 7; DL 1.1, 1.2) | Whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers, public records | Specific fair disclosure only; reject deemed disclosure | Delete 1.1 and 1.2 general disclosure. |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | No claim for matters Buyer knew or could discover from data room/public records | Delete blanket exclusion | Delete. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry; never for title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. |
| Bluefen (3 / 6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery" | Effective consent and evidence of conditions before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient | Make consent plus evidence of cl 11.3 conditions a Completion condition. Delete "satisfied on delivery." |
| Riverlark (2 / 7) | ~AUD 3.2m repaid by a release after Completion | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases; post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval | Require payout at Completion from funds flow and security release documents held in escrow. |
| Bonuses / funds flow | AUD 420k "a matter for the Seller," not in funds flow | Specific line item or Seller-funded; no silent exclusion | Add a specific line item or Seller-fund, with on-costs quantified. |
| Ironquay IP (11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden indemnity; preserve SOW3 cure | Broaden. Require payment and confirmatory assignment evidence pre-Completion. |
| DD-006 export/privacy | "Preliminary, not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way | Accept the factual disclosure, reject the materiality characterisation. Impose the investigation and reporting obligations. |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction | Reject "ordinary course" as settled. Assess terms and termination rights. No automatic Debt or price deduction. |
| Title (DD-012) | Share register evidences title | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence required | Reject. DD-012 is an internal source, not independent proof. |
| Tax / IP | "Settled under the general regime" | OPEN; no unlimited liability; no resolution | Reject "settled." Keep Tax and IP as separate categories. |

## 2. Reasoning on the material issues

**Fundamental/Title and the general regime.** The Seller's proposal to put capacity and title under the general caps and time limits is the most serious departure. It collapses the separate regime our playbook requires, which exists precisely because title defects are not a matter of ordinary warranty risk. Combined with the "applies to all Claims" override, it would subject title claims to the 4.8m cap, the 18-month period and the basket. We should treat this as a threshold issue: no progress on the caps until the Fundamental regime is restored.

**Thresholds (worked example).** For a AUD 300,000 breach claim:
- *Our playbook:* the claim clears the AUD 5,000 de minimis and the basket tips once aggregate claims exceed AUD 50,000, so the Seller pays from the first dollar: AUD 300,000 (subject to cap).
- *Seller's proposal:* the claim clears the AUD 25,000 de minimis, but only the excess above the AUD 250,000 basket is recoverable: AUD 50,000.

A AUD 20,000 claim is recoverable under our playbook once aggregate claims exceed AUD 50,000 (it counts toward the basket). Under the Seller's proposal it is not actionable at all. The Seller's package would leave the Buyer bearing the first AUD 250,000 of losses in almost every realistic scenario.

**Disclosure and buyer knowledge.** Section 1.1 discloses every fact in a 22 September data room, including DD-002 to DD-012, and 8.3 bars claims for anything discoverable from it. Together these would convert the data room into a general disclosure against all warranties. That is incompatible with specific fair disclosure. Clause 1.2 also purports to disclose the Accounts and public registers "without limiting any specific disclosure," which is circular. Our position is to delete both.

**Bluefen (~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue).** The disclosure letter confirms there is no final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. "Satisfied on delivery" would allow Completion before the consent is effective. Reasonable endeavours is expressly insufficient for a material customer consent under our playbook. This should be a condition precedent, not a covenant.

**Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m).** The Seller intends to deal with the facility by a post-Completion release. The disclosure confirms it has not been repaid and no discharge is included. Our playbook requires direct repayment from Completion funds; any post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Frost's approval. Separately, the price mechanics should confirm this debt is treated as Debt under the debt-free/cash-free basis. The Seller's documents do not show that.

**Bonuses (AUD 420k).** The Seller states the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not in the funds flow. Our playbook requires a specific line item or Seller-funding. The disclosure also says payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are unaddressed, and that the bonuses are conditional on continued employment. We need to know who bears the on-costs and what happens if the conditions are not met. Silent exclusion from the funds flow is not acceptable.

**Ironquay IP.** The Seller's indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment. The disclosure confirms DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of project materials on payment of every SOW3 fee, and that there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment. The AUD 180k figure (DD-010) is not independent bank verification of non-payment, and we should not treat it as either confirmed or disputed. The indemnity should be broadened to cover ownership and transfer defects, cure costs and third-party claims, while preserving the SOW3 cure mechanism.

**DD-006 export incident.** The Seller characterises this as not expected to be material, which is not supported by the disclosure: it records a possibly unauthorised download link covering ~1,240 records with personal information (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps), and the investigation is preliminary. Our playbook assumes no confirmed breach or notification duty and no loss amount. Practically, we should require log preservation, a defined investigation scope and regular updates before signing. We should ask privacy counsel to assess whether any notification obligation could arise under the Privacy Act, and whether a specific indemnity is warranted if the investigation later establishes a breach. We should not assert a breach ourselves.

**Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k).** The Seller calls these ordinary course. The disclosure confirms DD-008 and DD-011 must be read together, and does not say whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. We should assess the contracts before accepting either characterisation. Our playbook prohibits automatic Debt classification or a price deduction, so the assessment should drive any negotiation, not a default outcome.

**Title evidence.** The share register at DD-012 is an internal Company record and the Seller relies on it alone. Our playbook requires independent evidence. We should request an ASIC company extract, an independent register search, PPSR and encumbrance searches, and evidence of corporate authority for the sale (board and shareholder approvals).

**Items the playbook does not address.** The office lease (DD-007, notification obligation) and Mossvale (DD-009, assignment restriction) raise the question of whether landlord or counterparty consent is needed for a share sale. The Seller says it is not. The playbook is silent, so this should be confirmed by counsel on the actual documents. If consent is required, it should become a condition precedent. We should not create a new position on these without instructions.

## 3. Recommendations

**Must resolve before further negotiation (Tier 1)**
1. Reject the Fundamental/Title regime change. Restore 100% cap, six-year period, and carve-out from basket, de minimis and knowledge.
2. Add a non-waivable fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out to all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions.
3. Delete the general disclosure of the data room, Accounts and public registers (DL 1.1, 1.2, Sch. 7). Require specific fair disclosure.
4. Delete the buyer-knowledge bar (8.3).
5. Make the Bluefen consent and evidence of cl 11.3 conditions a condition precedent. Delete "satisfied on delivery."
6. Require Riverlark payout from Completion funds, with security releases in escrow.
7. Add the AUD 420k bonuses plus quantified on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded.
8. Obtain independent title evidence beyond DD-012.

**Negotiate with authority (Tier 2)**
9. Caps, thresholds and time limits: open at 25% / AUD 6m, AUD 5k de minimis, AUD 50k tipping basket, 24 months. Do not concede 20%/4.8m or 18 months without Amelia Frost's written approval identifying the draft.
10. Ironquay: broaden the indemnity; require payment and confirmatory assignment evidence before Completion.
11. DD-006: require log preservation, investigation scope, updates, and privacy counsel review. Consider a specific indemnity if a breach is later established.
12. Sandbar: assess the contracts. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.

**Clarify and confirm (Tier 3)**
13. Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009): counsel to confirm whether consent is required; add CP if so.
14. Tax and IP: reject "settled under the general regime." Keep them as separate categories, with terms open.
15. Request a bring-down of the disclosure letter to current date (5 November 2026), as the 22 September position may be out of date.
16. Tidy the clause cross-references. Several are inconsistent (e.g., conditions appear as cl 3, 6.3, 2 and 7).

**Authority reminder:** The Seller's 20%/AUD 4.8m cap and 18-month claims period are the conditional fallbacks. Neither may be conceded without Amelia Frost's prior written approval identifying the draft.
=== END ADVICE ===
